items.title: Trip summaries reach your backend
items.description: Every completed trip is stored once under its trip_id and sent with the next sync as a root `trips` array — start and end time, distance, duration, average speed, start and stop position. It is marked sent only when the request succeeds. Native trips are now recorded in every motion mode and from changePace().

items.title: Auto-sync drains the whole queue
items.description: Each trigger used to upload one batch and stop, and a fix recorded mid-upload scheduled nothing — with maxBatchSize: 1 the server replayed the route one point at a time. A single trigger now drains the backlog, and autoSyncThreshold, httpTimeout and the backoff settings are honoured.

items.title: Prod crash-model license keys work
items.description: A prod key no longer needs a Play Integrity token: it is bound to your app id (and Android signing cert) and unlocks on Android and iOS with no native setup. Create one from the license portal.

items.title: Android tracking that stays on — and stops when told
items.description: A reopened app no longer drops a parked session to periodic tracking, a restart after process death no longer gives up, a stopped stream can no longer keep GPS running until the battery dies, and crash detection works without the Physical activity permission.

items.title: iOS keeps streaming with the blue bar off
items.description: With Always permission and the indicator hidden, iOS 16.4+ suspended continuous tracking in the background. Tracelet now runs CoreLocation the way Apple requires to stay awake; your distanceFilter still decides what is recorded. Archives also ship dSYMs for the Rust frameworks.
